reply_text:
Starting the backfill. First, counting which records need it:163 records. Some are from this morning, after last night's fix, so I'm checking why those still lack ports before backfilling.These turns never received their reply (`happened`) from Emacs, so ports had nothing to compute from. Finding out why Emacs stopped posting it:The JVM already handles every status safely. So the fix is in Emacs: apply the `requested` gate only in `files` mode.Those three dispatch-test failures also fail without my change, so they're older. Next: planting the bug, then committing and loading it into Emacs.The `in-reply-to` filter is ignored, so I'll query by session instead and match locally.113 records settled. 50 had no reply I could match, including my own turn from this morning, so I'm checking why before calling those lost.kimi-1 built the turn-to-acts adapter, so it's the best-placed seat for this. I'm sending it a discovery-only packet.㊥ (`"please do those 2 unresolved actions"`) Both are under way. The backfill is done: 136 of the 163 records missing ports now have them. While doing it I found and fixed the reason this morning's turns had none (futon3c `6f0a2316`, loaded into Emacs). The discovery pass for recording bells as turns is running on kimi-1. It's parked, so I'll report when it bells back.

㊩ (the second cause) Emacs only sent a turn's reply to the JVM if 象 hadn't read the turn yet. Since 象 now reads when you send, a reply that takes longer than the reading was never sent. That's nearly every working turn, so since 03:08 today no reply text was stored, and no commits or ports either. claude-7's demo escaped because its replies were quick.
- **The fix:** Emacs now also sends the reply for turns already read. Turns with 象 switched off still never contact the JVM, which an existing test requires.
- **Checks:** a new test, plus a planted bug that it catches. Three older tests in `session-turn-analysis-dispatch-test` already fail without my change, and I haven't touched them.

㊢ (backfill)
- **Where the replies came from:** each record's reply was taken from the stored text (70), or found in the evidence store (68).
- **How it ran:** one record at a time, one second apart, through the same route Emacs uses. futon1b stayed healthy throughout.
- **Matching replies:** an agent's reply often doesn't point back at the operator turn it answers; its `in-reply-to` can be a tool step. So I matched the remaining replies by order within the session.
- **The 25 left over:** 23 of them have no operator evidence id, so there's nothing to look them up by.
- **What's still missing:** commits for the backfilled turns. The snapshot taken at the end of each turn is gone, so none of these turns will show a commit closing anything.

㊯ (discovery) kimi-1 has the packet. Job `invoke-1791183050805-32677-0bf5f12b`, park `park-489c8b9b`, deadline 45 minutes. It doesn't change any code. It answers four questions in `holes/excursions/E-agency-work-orders-bells-discovery.md`:
- **Hook points:** where bells, whistles and auto-bellbacks are accepted and where their jobs end, with the fields available at each.
- **Volume:** bells and whistles per day.
- **Linking:** which existing fields let a bell point at the request it relays. The worked example is the claude-4 → codex-23 capture packet.
- **Cost:** what reading the bells with 象 would cost, compared with reading marks classically.

When it reports, I'll check the note and bring you a proposed build packet.
